definitions.explanation: The time of day when light first appears in the sky; the beginning of morning.
The start of a new era, period, or development.

examples.japanese: {夜明|よあ}けの{空|そら}が{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The sky at dawn was beautiful.

examples.japanese: {夜明|よあ}け{前|まえ}が{一番|いちばん}{暗|くら}い。
examples.notes: A common saying meaning things are worst just before they get better

examples.japanese: {夜明|よあ}けとともに{鳥|とり}が{鳴|な}き{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The birds started singing with the break of dawn.
examples.notes: 夜明けとともに = at dawn, with the break of day

examples.japanese: {登山|とざん}{者|しゃ}たちは{夜明|よあ}け{前|まえ}に{出発|しゅっぱつ}し、{山頂|さんちょう}で{日|ひ}の{出|で}を{見|み}た。
examples.english: The climbers departed before dawn and saw the sunrise from the summit.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{時代|じだい}の{夜明|よあ}けだ。
examples.english: It's the dawn of a new era.

examples.japanese: {民主主義|みんしゅしゅぎ}の{夜明|よあ}けを{告|つ}げる{出来事|できごと}だった。
examples.english: It was an event that heralded the dawn of democracy.

examples.japanese: {科学|かがく}{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{夜明|よあ}けとも{言|い}える{発見|はっけん}だ。
examples.english: It's a discovery that could be called the dawn of science and technology.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{戦争|せんそう}が{終|お}わり、{平和|へいわ}の{夜明|よあ}けがようやく{訪|おとず}れた。
examples.english: The long war ended, and the dawn of peace finally arrived.

examples.japanese: あの{革命|かくめい}は、{古|ふる}い{体制|たいせい}が{崩|くず}れ、{新|あたら}しい{社会|しゃかい}の{夜明|よあ}けとなった{歴史|れきし}{的|てき}な{転換点|てんかんてん}だった。
examples.english: That revolution was a historic turning point where the old system collapsed and became the dawn of a new society.

notes:
USAGE: {夜明|よあ}け refers to the time when the sky begins to lighten. It can also be used figuratively to mean the beginning of something new.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{夜明|よあ}け{前|まえ} (before dawn)
・{夜明|よあ}けとともに (at dawn, with the break of day)
・〜の{夜明|よあ}け (the dawn of ~)

SIMILAR WORDS:
・{明|あ}け{方|がた} - early morning, dawn
・{暁|あかつき} - dawn (literary)
・{日|ひ}の{出|で} - sunrise
